question: Where the Fed NPRM goes beyond restating the statute, which capital, liquidity and reserve requirements add numbers or deadlines the Act does not contain?
author: planned by Claude Code (claude-fable-5-1)

program.title: Fed GENIUS NPRM: numbers and deadlines beyond the Act
program.thesis: Classify each Fed NPRM and GENIUS Act paragraph by prudential topic and whether it states a concrete number or deadline, then pair NPRM requirements with their closest statutory provisions to see which NPRM quantities and time limits have no counterpart in the Act.

unit.rationale: Numbers and deadlines live in individual obligations; paragraph units from the NPRM and the Act let each proposed requirement be compared with the statutory text it implements.

doc_notes.note: Federal Reserve Board proposed rule (2026) implementing the Board's responsibilities under the GENIUS Act (Public Law 119-27, 'the Act'). Covers payment stablecoin issuers supervised by the Board, including subsidiaries of state member banks; proposes text in 12 CFR Parts 208, 211, 217, 247 (Regulation UU) and 263. Proposed, not yet binding.

GENIUS Act, Public Law 119-27, enacted July 18, 2025: the statute governing permitted payment stablecoin issuers. It sets reserve, redemption, disclosure and supervisory requirements and directs regulators to issue capital, liquidity and risk-management rules. This is 'the Act' that the Fed NPRM implements.

nodes.label: Prudential requirement
nodes.question: Does this paragraph state or define a requirement, limit or standard concerning capital, liquidity, or reserves backing payment stablecoins (including reserve composition, custody, redemption timing, or reserve reporting/attestation)? See scope_note.
nodes.why: Cheap gate to the three topics the question asks about.

nodes.label: Prudential topic
nodes.question: Which prudential topic does this paragraph mainly address?

options.description: Capital requirements, capital ratios, buffers, minimum capital amounts
Liquidity requirements, liquid asset buffers, redemption timing and liquidity risk management
What assets may back the stablecoin, the 1:1 backing ratio, maturity or concentration limits
Segregation, custody, rehypothecation or pledging of reserves
Reserve disclosure, monthly reports, attestations, examinations or certifications
Some other prudential matter or none of the above

nodes.why: Groups findings by capital, liquidity and reserve subtopics and blocks pairing.

nodes.label: States a number
nodes.question: Does this paragraph state a specific quantitative threshold or parameter (a percentage, ratio, dollar amount, maturity in days, count, or cap)? Ignore section numbers, citations and dates of enactment.

nodes.label: States a deadline
nodes.question: Does this paragraph set a specific deadline, time limit, or frequency for doing something (e.g. within N days, monthly, annually, by a stated date)?
nodes.why: Identifies time-bound requirements; more targeted than the base deadline field.

nodes.label: Quantity type
nodes.question: What kind of specific figure or time element does this paragraph mainly contain?

options.description: A percentage or ratio (e.g. capital ratio, backing ratio, concentration limit)
A dollar amount or size threshold
A maturity limit or duration of an asset or instrument
A time limit to act, such as redeeming, notifying, or curing a shortfall
A recurring frequency such as daily, monthly, quarterly, annual
No specific figure or time element

nodes.why: Shows what sort of specifics are present.

nodes.label: Relation to Act
nodes.question: Using scope_note, how does this Fed proposed-rule paragraph present its requirement relative to the GENIUS Act?

options.description: Repeats or closely paraphrases what the Act itself requires, or cites the Act as setting this requirement
Fills in detail (a number, deadline, method or definition) for a requirement the Act states only in general terms or delegates to regulators
Imposes a requirement the Board adds on its own authority, not traceable to a specific statutory requirement
Cannot be told from the paragraph

nodes.why: Single-unit estimate of whether the NPRM goes beyond restating; corroborated by the pairwise relation.

nodes.label: Specificity
nodes.question: How concrete is the requirement in this paragraph?
levels: Qualitative standard with no figures or timing
Names a figure or timing but leaves it to be determined later or case by case
States one explicit number or deadline
States multiple explicit numbers, deadlines or a full formula
nodes.why: Lets the NPRM's concreteness be compared with the Act's by topic.

relations.label: NPRM vs Act
relations.question: A and B are prudential provisions, one from the Fed proposed rule and one from the GENIUS Act. How does the proposed-rule provision relate to the statutory provision?

options.description: Both address the same requirement and the Act already contains the same number or deadline the rule states (or neither has one): the rule restates the statute
Both address the same requirement, but the rule states a number, threshold, deadline or frequency that the statutory provision does not contain
Both address the same requirement and both state a number or deadline, but the values differ
They address different requirements

views.title: NPRM prudential paragraphs going beyond the Act with a number or deadline
views.why: Headline count of proposed requirements that specify or add to the statute.

views.title: NPRM: topic by relation to the Act
views.why: Shows which of capital, liquidity and reserve topics are restated versus specified or newly added.

views.title: What kind of numbers and deadlines the NPRM adds, by topic
views.why: Breaks the additions into ratios, dollar amounts, maturities, deadlines and frequencies.

views.title: Mean specificity: Act vs NPRM by topic
views.why: Where the NPRM is markedly more concrete than the Act, it is supplying the figures.

views.title: NPRM provisions linked to Act provisions
views.why: Shows which statutory provisions each proposed requirement matches, adds to or departs from.

views.title: NPRM requirements with numbers or deadlines beyond the Act
views.why: The actual paragraphs to read, most concrete first.
